mainTopic: Meat slaughtered or food cooked for a sick person on שבת; which tools are valid for שחיטה, including blades attached to the ground
overview: The amud opens by finishing a discussion about eating, on שבת, meat from an animal slaughtered that day. The meat can be permitted if a dangerously sick person was in the house before שבת, because then the live animal was never מוקצה. רבי יהודה forbids it when the sick person recovered. רב rules that meat slaughtered for a sick person is forbidden to a healthy person, but cooked food is permitted, because raw food was fit to chew and a live animal was not. רב פפא shows that the real question is whether the food was usable when שבת began. רב דימי gives the final הלכה, which is the opposite: the meat is permitted raw to a healthy person, and cooked food is forbidden in case the cook adds extra. Then a new משנה teaches which tools may be used for שחיטה. Any tool that cuts cleanly is fine, but tools that strangle are not. The גמרא works through a debate between רבי and רבי חייא about blades attached to the ground. It concludes that a blade attached from the start is invalid, while a loose blade later fixed in place is valid, and it proves this from a ברייתא.

steps.title: There was a sick person in the house before שבת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains why the meat is not מוקצה for the view that allows eating it on שבת. A dangerously sick person was already in the house before שבת began.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is talking about a case where he had a sick person in his house while it was still day, before שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers a question from just before this section: how can anyone allow eating this meat on שבת if a live animal is מוקצה? It answers that there was already a sick person in the house before שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A live animal normally cannot be used on שבת, so a person sets his mind away from it and it becomes מוקצה. But if a dangerously sick person was in the house when שבת began, the animal might well be slaughtered for him. So the owner never set his mind away from it, and it is not מוקצה.

keyTerms.meaning: A sick person; here, someone dangerously ill, for whom one may slaughter even on שבת
While it was still day, meaning before שבת began
Something set aside and not usable on שבת because one did not have it in mind for use when שבת began

phrases.english: For example, where he had a sick person
phrases.notes: He means a dangerously sick person, for whom it is allowed to slaughter even on שבת.

phrases.english: while it was still day.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּגוֹן שֶׁהָיָה לוֹ חוֹלֶה מִבְּעוֹד יוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers a question raised just before this section about how the meat can avoid being מוקצה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A live animal is always מוקצה on שבת, so its meat should never be allowed that day.
steps.terutzMaskana: If a sick person was there before שבת, the animal was ready to be slaughtered for him, so it was never set aside.

steps.title: Then why does רבי יהודה forbid it?
steps.stepSummary: If the animal was never מוקצה, the גמרא asks what reason רבי יהודה could have for forbidding the meat on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, what is the reason of רבי יהודה, who forbids it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer it just gave. If there was a sick person and the animal was not מוקצה, why would רבי יהודה forbid eating it on שבת?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case was set up so that מוקצה does not apply. But רבי יהודה forbids the meat, and his reason was supposed to be מוקצה. Now that reason seems to be gone, so his ruling needs a new explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: If so; used to show that an answer causes a new problem
What is the reason?
He forbade

phrases.english: If so,
what is the reason of Rabbi Yehuda, who forbids it?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה דְּאָסַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the case described in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The setup of step 1, a sick person before שבת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the animal was not מוקצה, nothing is left to explain רבי יהודה's ban.

steps.title: The sick person recovered
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה is talking about a case where the sick person got better, so the slaughtering was not allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is talking about a case where he had a sick person and the person got better.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי יהודה is discussing a case where there was a sick person before שבת, but that person recovered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The animal was not מוקצה when שבת began, because of the sick person. But once the person recovered, there was no permission to slaughter, so the slaughtering was a forbidden act done by mistake. For that reason רבי יהודה forbids eating the meat on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: And he recovered, became healthy

phrases.english: For example, where he had a sick person
and he recovered.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 2.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If the animal was not מוקצה, רבי יהודה has no reason to forbid it.
steps.terutzMaskana: After the recovery, slaughtering was not allowed, so it was a mistaken forbidden act, and רבי יהודה forbids the meat.

steps.title: רב's rule: slaughtered for the sick is forbidden to the healthy, cooked is permitted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that רב silenced the תנא because of his own rule. Meat slaughtered for a sick person on שבת is forbidden to a healthy person, but food cooked for a sick person is permitted to a healthy person.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like what רב אחא בר אדא said in the name of רב, and some say רבי יצחק בר אדא said it in the name of רב: if someone slaughters for a sick person on שבת, the meat is forbidden to a healthy person. If someone cooks for a sick person on שבת, the food is permitted to a healthy person.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that רב's earlier silencing of the תנא fits a rule רב taught elsewhere. It then quotes that rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב holds that a live animal is מוקצה for a healthy person, even when it was slaughtered permitted, for a sick person. Food that is cooked does not have this problem. This explains why רב did not accept a teaching that ignored the מוקצה problem of a slaughtered animal.

keyTerms.meaning: One who slaughters
A healthy person
One who cooks

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the slaughtering itself was wrong. Slaughtering for the sick person is fully allowed. The ban for the healthy person comes only from מוקצה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This rule becomes a key source for the difference between meat slaughtered and food cooked for a sick person on שבת.

phrases.english: And it is like that which said
phrases.notes: This explains why רב silenced the תנא earlier: it fits his own rule quoted here.

phrases.aramaic: רַב אַחָא בַּר אַדָּא אָמַר רַב,
phrases.english: Rav Aḥa bar Adda, in the name of Rav,
and some say

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק בַּר אַדָּא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzḥak bar Adda said in the name of Rav:
One who slaughters for a sick person on Shabbat,
it is forbidden to a healthy person;
one who cooks for a sick person on Shabbat,
it is permitted to a healthy person.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי הָא דְּאָמַר רַב אַחָא בַּר אַדָּא אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to explaining רב's silencing of the תנא, now backed by רב's own rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Meat slaughtered on שבת for a sick person is forbidden to a healthy person; food cooked for a sick person is permitted to a healthy person.

steps.title: Why the difference?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why slaughtered meat and cooked food are treated differently.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind רב's split ruling. This sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In both cases a forbidden act was done for a sick person, and was allowed. So it is not clear why the result for a healthy person should be different.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind step 4.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why slaughtered meat is forbidden to a healthy person but cooked food is permitted.

steps.title: Raw food could be chewed; a live animal could not
steps.stepSummary: Raw food was fit to chew before שבת, so it was never מוקצה. A live animal was not fit to chew, so it was מוקצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: This one (the food) was fit to chew, and that one (the animal) was not fit to chew.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains רב's distinction. Raw food was already edible in some way, while a live animal was not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Raw food can be chewed even before cooking, so a person never set his mind away from it when שבת began. A live animal cannot be eaten at all until it is slaughtered, so it was מוקצה for a healthy person. The slaughtering for the sick person does not remove that status for the healthy person.

keyTerms.meaning: Fit to chew; edible even raw
Not fit

steps.whatToRemember: Food cooked for a sick person on שבת is permitted to a healthy person, because it was edible raw. Meat slaughtered for him is forbidden to a healthy person, because a live animal was מוקצה.

phrases.english: This one was fit to chew,
phrases.notes: "This one" is the food that was cooked; it could be chewed even raw.

phrases.english: and that one was not fit to chew.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַאי רָאוּי לָכוֹס, וְהַאי אֵינוֹ רָאוּי לָכוֹס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Raw food was fit to chew before שבת and so was not מוקצה; a live animal was not fit to chew and so was מוקצה.

steps.title: Sometimes the slaughtered meat is permitted and the cooked food is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא shows that רב's rule depends on מוקצה. If the sick person was already sick before שבת, the meat is permitted. If the vegetable was picked on שבת, the cooked food is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא says: Sometimes meat slaughtered for a sick person is permitted, for example when the person was already sick before שבת. Sometimes cooked food is forbidden, for example when a gourd was cut off the ground for him on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא takes the reason from Step 6, which is מוקצה, and shows that it can flip the results of רב's rule in certain cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the person was sick before שבת began, the owner already had the animal in mind for possible slaughter, so it was never מוקצה. If a gourd was still attached to the ground when שבת started, it was not usable then, so it is מוקצה even after it is cooked. So the question is not 'slaughtered or cooked'. The question is whether the food was usable when שבת started.

keyTerms.meaning: Sometimes; there are times when
Cut off, detached from the ground
A gourd, a type of squash

phrases.english: Rav Pappa says:
There are times when one who slaughters, the meat is permitted,

phrases.aramaic: כְּגוֹן שֶׁהָיָה לוֹ חוֹלֶה מִבְּעוֹד יוֹם;
phrases.english: such as where he had a sick person while it was still day;
phrases.notes: The person was already sick before שבת, so the animal was ready to be used for him. It was never מוקצה.

phrases.english: and one who cooks, the food is forbidden,
such as where he cut a gourd for him.
phrases.notes: The gourd was picked off the ground on שבת, so it could not be used when שבת began.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: פְּעָמִים שֶׁהַשּׁוֹחֵט מוּתָּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the מוקצה reason from Step 6 to show exceptions to רב's rule from Step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The result depends on whether the food was usable before שבת. A person sick from before שבת makes the meat permitted. A gourd cut on שבת makes the cooked food forbidden.

steps.title: Final הלכה: meat slaughtered for a sick person is permitted raw to a healthy person
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי rules that a healthy person may eat, raw, the meat slaughtered for a sick person on שבת. The whole animal had to be slaughtered for the sick person anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב דימי of נהרדעא says the הלכה is: If someone slaughters for a sick person on שבת, a healthy person may eat the meat raw. Why? You cannot get even a כזית of meat without slaughtering the whole animal. So when he slaughters, he is slaughtering only for the sick person.
steps.whatsHappening: רב דימי gives the final הלכה about slaughtering, and it goes against רב's rule from Step 4.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The slaughter was fully permitted, and it could not have been done any smaller. So nothing extra was done for the healthy person, and the meat does not become forbidden. He may eat it only raw, because cooking it for himself on שבת would be a new forbidden act.

keyTerms.meaning: The final practical הלכה
Raw meat
An olive-sized amount, the smallest amount that counts as eating
With the intention of, for the sake of

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with רב in Step 4. רב said slaughtered meat is forbidden and cooked food is permitted. The final הלכה here is the exact opposite.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical הלכה, and it replaces רב's rule.

phrases.english: Rav Dimi of Neharde'a says: The halakha is:
One who slaughters for a sick person on Shabbat,
it is permitted for a healthy person raw.
What is the reason?

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן דְּאִי אֶפְשָׁר לִכְזַיִת בָּשָׂר בְּלֹא שְׁחִיטָה,
phrases.english: Since it is impossible to have an olive-bulk of meat without slaughter,
when he slaughters,
he slaughters with the sick person in mind.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the final ruling, which goes against רב's rule in Step 4.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Meat slaughtered for a sick person on שבת is permitted raw to a healthy person, because the whole slaughter was done for the sick person.

steps.title: Final הלכה: food cooked for a sick person is forbidden to a healthy person
steps.stepSummary: Food cooked for a sick person on שבת is forbidden to a healthy person. This is a rabbinic decree, so that the cook does not make extra food for the healthy person.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone cooks for a sick person on שבת, the food is forbidden to a healthy person. This is a decree, in case he cooks more because of the healthy person.
steps.whatsHappening: רב דימי finishes his ruling with the cooking case and gives its reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Cooking is different from slaughtering, because you can cook any amount you want. If healthy people were allowed to eat the food, the cook might add extra for them. So the חכמים forbade it.

keyTerms.meaning: A protective rabbinic decree
Lest he add more

steps.whatToRemember: Final הלכה: slaughtered meat is permitted (raw) to a healthy person, but cooked food is forbidden to him, because of the decree that he might add more.

phrases.english: One who cooks for a sick person on Shabbat,
it is forbidden for a healthy person,
a decree lest he add more on his account.
phrases.notes: 'His account' means the healthy person: the cook might throw in extra food for him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב דימי's ruling with the cooking case.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Cooked food for a sick person is forbidden to a healthy person, because of the decree that he might cook more.

steps.title: New משנה: slaughtering with a hand sickle, flint or reed is valid
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה rules that שחיטה done with a hand sickle, a sharpened flint, or a reed is valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If someone slaughters with a hand sickle, a flint, or a reed, his slaughter is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now moves to a new משנה about which tools may be used for שחיטה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: None of these is a regular knife, but each one can make a smooth cut. The משנה teaches that the tool does not have to be metal. It only has to cut properly.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for מתניתין, our משנה
A hand sickle
A sharpened flint stone
A reed
Valid

phrases.english: MISHNA:
One who slaughters with a hand sickle,
phrases.notes: He means the smooth side of the sickle.

phrases.english: with a flint, or with a reed,
his slaughter is valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שחיטה with a hand sickle, a flint or a reed is valid.

steps.title: Anyone, any time, any cutting tool, except tools that strangle
steps.stepSummary: The משנה states a general rule: anyone may slaughter, at any time, with anything. The exceptions are a harvest sickle, a saw, teeth and a fingernail, because they strangle the animal instead of cutting.
steps.simpleTranslation: Everyone may slaughter, one may always slaughter, and one may slaughter with anything. The exceptions are a harvest sickle, a saw, teeth and a fingernail, because they strangle.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a broad rule for שחיטה and then lists the tools that do not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These tools are jagged or blunt, so they tear and choke the animal instead of making a clean cut. Strangling is not שחיטה. The general rule is that any tool works as long as it cuts smoothly.

keyTerms.meaning: A harvest sickle with a serrated edge
A saw
A fingernail
They strangle or choke

steps.whatToRemember: A valid שחיטה needs a clean cut. Tools that tear or choke are not valid.

phrases.english: All may slaughter,
and one may always slaughter,
phrases.notes: He means at any time, day or night.

phrases.english: and one may slaughter with anything,
except for a harvest sickle,
and a saw, and teeth,
and a fingernail,
because they strangle.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַכֹּל שׁוֹחֲטִין, וּלְעוֹלָם שׁוֹחֲטִין, וּבַכֹּל שׁוֹחֲטִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה with a general rule and its exceptions.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Anyone may slaughter, at any time, with any cutting tool, except tools that strangle: a harvest sickle, a saw, teeth and a fingernail.

steps.title: The משנה's wording means 'only after the fact'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that the משנה says 'one who slaughters' rather than 'one may slaughter.' This means the שחיטה is valid only בדיעבד, not לכתחילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: The משנה says 'one who slaughters,' so after the fact, yes, it is valid. From the start, no, one should not do it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by reading something into the exact wording of the משנה. It sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'הַשּׁוֹחֵט' describes something that already happened. So the משנה is telling us the שחיטה works once it was done (דיעבד). It is not giving permission to plan to do it this way (לכתחילה).

keyTerms.meaning: After the fact; once it has already been done
From the start; as the proper way to do it
One who slaughters (describes a done act, not a permission)

steps.confusionAlert: Valid בדיעבד does not mean forbidden or invalid. The meat is kosher; you just should not plan to slaughter this way.

phrases.english: GEMARA: 'One who slaughters':
after the fact, yes; from the start, no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the משנה from step 10 by analyzing its wording.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Slaughtering with a hand sickle, flint or reed is valid only בדיעבד.

steps.title: Flint and reed are allowed from the start in a ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: For a hand sickle, 'only בדיעבד' makes sense, since one might use its jagged side. But a ברייתא allows flint and reed with no limit, which contradicts reading the משנה as 'בדיעבד only.'
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense for a hand sickle: maybe he will come to slaughter with the other side. But flint and reed are not allowed from the start? A ברייתא contradicts this: 'We may slaughter with anything: with flint, with glass, or with the stalk of a reed.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts the 'בדיעבד only' reading for the hand sickle. It then challenges that reading for flint and reed, using a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A hand sickle has one smooth edge and one jagged edge, so there is a real worry about using the wrong side. A flint or reed has no jagged side, so why limit it? The ברייתא says 'בכל שוחטין', which sounds like full permission from the start.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted; it makes sense that... (sets up a contrast)
The other side (the jagged edge of the sickle)
A sharpened flint stone
The hard outer stalk of a reed

phrases.english: Granted, with a hand sickle,
perhaps he will come to do it with the other side,
phrases.notes: The other side of a hand sickle is jagged like a harvest sickle, and step 11 said those strangle instead of cut.

phrases.english: but flint and reed are not allowed from the start?
And raise a contradiction: 'We may slaughter with anything,
whether with flint, whether with glass,
whether with the stalk of a reed!'

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא בְּמַגַּל יָד דִּלְמָא אָתֵי לְמֶעְבַּד בְּאִידַּךְ גִּיסָא אֶלָּא צוֹר וְקָנֶה לְכִתְחִלָּה לָא? וּרְמִינְהִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the 'בדיעבד only' reading from step 12 for flint and reed.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that flint and reed are valid only בדיעבד.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Flint and reed have no jagged side, and a ברייתא allows them לכתחילה ('בכל שוחטין').

steps.title: Detached versus attached to the ground
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא is talking about a flint or reed that is detached. The משנה is talking about one still attached to the ground.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. Here it means detached; there it means attached.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction by saying the two sources describe different cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A loose flint or a cut reed is just a normal tool, and the ברייתא allows it לכתחילה. If the flint or reed is attached to the ground, it is a different case. For that case the משנה allows it only בדיעבד.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult (introduces an answer)
Detached from the ground
Attached to the ground

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
here, when detached; here, when attached.
phrases.notes: The first 'here' is the ברייתא, which allows it from the start. The second 'here' is our משנה, which allows it only after the fact.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: כָּאן בְּתָלוּשׁ, כָּאן בִּמְחוּבָּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): each source refers to a different situation.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה and ברייתא seemed to discuss the same flint and reed.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is about attached ones (בדיעבד only); the ברייתא is about detached ones (allowed לכתחילה).

steps.title: Support from רב כהנא's report of a debate
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא reports that רבי says slaughtering with an attached blade is invalid, and רבי חייא says it is valid. The גמרא reads this to mean רבי חייא allows it only בדיעבד, which matches the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב כהנא said: one who slaughters with something attached to the ground, רבי says it is invalid and רבי חייא says it is valid. רבי חייא only says it is valid after the fact, but not from the start.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source to show that attached blades are valid only בדיעבד. This supports the answer in step 14.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חייא's word 'מכשיר' (valid) is read as a ruling about something already done. So even the lenient opinion does not allow attached blades לכתחילה. This fits the משנה's 'הַשּׁוֹחֵט'.

keyTerms.meaning: Rules invalid
Rules valid
He only rules it valid in this case (limits a ruling)

phrases.english: As Rav Kahana said:
one who slaughters with something attached to the ground:
Rabbi rules it invalid and Rabbi Ḥiyya rules it valid;

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא קָא מַכְשִׁיר רַבִּי חִיָּיא
phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥiyya rules it valid
only after the fact, but not from the start.
phrases.notes: This is the גמרא's own reading of רבי חייא, not part of רב כהנא's words.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Backs up step 14's answer with an existing debate.
steps.raayaObject: That an attached blade is valid only בדיעבד, matching the משנה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב כהנא's report of the debate between רבי and רבי חייא.

steps.title: A ברייתא that fits neither רבי nor רבי חייא
steps.stepSummary: If רבי חייא allows attached blades only בדיעבד, a ברייתא that fully allows attached blades fits no one. רבי חייא would not allow it לכתחילה, and רבי would not allow it even בדיעבד.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to whom did you explain the משנה? According to רבי חייא, and only after the fact? Then whose view is this ברייתא: 'We may slaughter with anything, detached or attached, knife above and neck below, or knife below and neck above'? Neither רבי nor רבי חייא! If רבי חייא, after the fact yes, from the start no. If רבי, even after the fact no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the way it explained רבי חייא in step 15, using a different ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ברייתא says 'בכל שוחטין', which means permission from the start, even with an attached blade. Under step 15's reading, רבי חייא allows it only בדיעבד, and רבי forbids it completely. So the ברייתא would have no author.

keyTerms.meaning: How did you set up (explain) the source?
Whose opinion is it?
The animal's neck

phrases.english: In accordance with whom did you set it up?
According to Rabbi Ḥiyya, and only after the fact?
But then, that which was taught in a baraita:

phrases.aramaic: בַּכֹּל שׁוֹחֲטִין, בֵּין בְּתָלוּשׁ בֵּין בִּמְחוּבָּר,
phrases.english: 'We may slaughter with anything, whether detached or attached,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין שֶׁהַסַּכִּין לְמַעְלָה וְצַוַּאר בְּהֵמָה לְמַטָּה,
phrases.english: whether the knife is above and the animal's neck below,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין שֶׁהַסַּכִּין לְמַטָּה וְצַוַּאר בְּהֵמָה לְמַעְלָה –
phrases.english: or the knife is below and the animal's neck above':

phrases.aramaic: מַנִּי? לָא רַבִּי וְלָא רַבִּי חִיָּיא!
phrases.english: whose view is it? Neither Rabbi nor Rabbi Ḥiyya!

phrases.aramaic: אִי רַבִּי חִיָּיא – דִּיעֲבַד אִין, לְכִתְחִלָּה לָא;
phrases.english: If Rabbi Ḥiyya: after the fact yes, from the start no;
if Rabbi: even after the fact, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּמַאי אוֹקֵימְתַּהּ כְּרַבִּי חִיָּיא וְדִיעֲבַד? אֶלָּא הָא דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 15's claim that רבי חייא allows attached blades only בדיעבד.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that רבי חייא permits attached blades only בדיעבד.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא permits attached blades לכתחילה. Under that reading neither רבי nor רבי חייא could be its author.

steps.title: רבי חייא allows it even from the start
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא follows רבי חייא, who really allows attached blades even לכתחילה. The debate was written about דיעבד only to show how strict רבי is.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, it is רבי חייא, and he allows it even from the start. The reason they argue about after the fact is to show you how far רבי goes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by taking back the claim that רבי חייא allows it only בדיעבד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'מכשיר' does not limit רבי חייא to דיעבד. The argument was framed as 'valid or invalid after the fact' to show the strength of רבי's view: he invalidates it even when it is already done. So the ברייתא has an author, רבי חייא.

keyTerms.meaning: Actually; really (keeps an earlier position and explains it)
They argue
To show you the strength (how far) of someone's opinion goes

steps.whatToRemember: An attached flint or reed: רבי says invalid even בדיעבד. רבי חייא allows it even לכתחילה. The argument is framed around דיעבד only to show how strict רבי is.
steps.confusionAlert: This answer takes away the support from step 15. רבי חייא no longer means 'only בדיעבד', so the משנה's 'בדיעבד only' cannot rest on him that way anymore.

phrases.english: Actually it is Rabbi Ḥiyya, and even from the start;
and the fact that they argue about after the fact
is to show you the strength of Rabbi's view.
phrases.notes: רבי invalidates it even when it is already done, and that is a bigger חידוש than just saying 'don't do it.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 16 by reinterpreting רבי חייא's position from step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting an opinion: the דיעבד framing describes רבי's strength, not a limit on רבי חייא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי חייא allows attached blades only בדיעבד.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי חייא allows attached blades even לכתחילה, so the ברייתא follows him.

steps.title: Now the משנה fits no one
steps.stepSummary: If רבי חייא allows attached blades even לכתחילה, and רבי forbids them even בדיעבד, then the משנה's 'בדיעבד yes, לכתחילה no' matches neither of them.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then our משנה, which says 'one who slaughters' (meaning: after the fact yes, from the start no), whose view is it? It is neither רבי nor רבי חייא. רבי חייא allows it even from the start. רבי does not allow it even after the fact.
steps.whatsHappening: The answer in the last step fixed the problem with the ברייתא, but it created a new problem. Now the משנה has no author.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 17 we said רבי חייא allows attached blades fully, even לכתחילה. The משנה's wording 'השוחט' suggests only בדיעבד. So it can't be רבי חייא, who is more lenient. It can't be רבי either, who is stricter and says invalid even בדיעבד.

keyTerms.meaning: But rather; then how about... (moves the problem onto another source)
If it is this one... if it is that one...

phrases.english: But rather, our mishna, which teaches "one who slaughters,"
phrases.notes: The word 'one who slaughters' sounds like it already happened. That is why the גמרא reads it as 'only after the fact.'

phrases.english: after the fact, yes; from the outset, no. Whose view is this?
It is neither Rabbi nor Rabbi Chiyya.
If Rabbi Chiyya, he allows it even from the outset.
If Rabbi, he does not allow it even after the fact.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the consequence of step 17's answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading in step 17 that רבי חייא allows attached blades even לכתחילה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Once רבי חייא is fully lenient and רבי is fully strict, nobody holds the middle position the משנה seems to teach.

steps.title: The משנה follows רבי
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא really does allow it even לכתחילה, and the משנה follows רבי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, the ברייתא follows רבי חייא, who allows it even from the start. And our משנה, which says 'one who slaughters,' follows רבי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps its view of רבי חייא and assigns the משנה to רבי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of changing what רבי חייא holds, the גמרא says the משנה's 'בדיעבד yes' comes from רבי. This answer seems odd, since רבי called attached blades invalid. The next step raises exactly that problem.

keyTerms.meaning: It follows the view of רבי

phrases.english: Actually, the ruling is Rabbi Chiyya's, and he allows it even from the outset,
phrases.notes: This means the ברייתא that fully allows attached blades follows רבי חייא, as step 17 said.

phrases.english: and our mishna, which teaches "one who slaughters," follows Rabbi.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 18 by assigning the משנה to רבי.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה can't be רבי, because he invalidates attached blades even בדיעבד.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is רבי. How this fits his other statement is worked out next.

steps.title: רבי contradicts himself
steps.stepSummary: If the משנה is רבי, then רבי contradicts himself: here he says valid בדיעבד, and in the debate with רבי חייא he says invalid.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then there is a contradiction between one statement of רבי and another statement of רבי!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out the obvious problem with the last answer: רבי now holds two opposite positions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the report of רב כהנא, רבי said slaughtering with an attached blade is invalid. Now the משנה, also רבי, says it is valid בדיעבד. Both can't be true unless the cases are different.

keyTerms.meaning: It is difficult: a problem
רבי's statement against רבי's other statement: a self-contradiction
Against: one source set against another

phrases.english: Then Rabbi's statement contradicts Rabbi's other statement!
phrases.notes: One statement is his ruling against רבי חייא in step 15. The other is the משנה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks step 19's answer.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי called attached blades invalid, but the משנה (now רבי) calls them valid בדיעבד.

steps.title: Attached from the start vs. reattached
steps.stepSummary: There is no contradiction. A blade attached from the start is invalid. A blade that was detached and later attached is valid בדיעבד.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. Here, where it was attached from the start, it is invalid. There, where it was detached and later he attached it, it is valid after the fact.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא solves רבי's contradiction by saying his two rulings are about two different kinds of attached blades.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Something that grew or formed attached to the ground, like a stone sticking out of the earth, is one case. Something that was loose and then fixed into the ground or wall is a different case. רבי invalidates the first and allows the second בדיעבד.

keyTerms.meaning: Attached from the start: it was always part of the ground
Detached, and later he attached it
Here... there...: the two rulings deal with different cases

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי: a blade attached from the start is invalid. A blade that was detached and then attached is valid בדיעבד (the משנה's case).
steps.confusionAlert: 'Attached' is not one single category here. The key question is whether it was always attached, or was loose first and then attached.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
here, it is a case where it was attached from the start,
phrases.notes: This is the debate with רבי חייא, where רבי says invalid.

phrases.english: there, it is a case where it was detached and in the end he attached it.
phrases.notes: This is our משנה, where רבי says valid after the fact.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 20 by splitting the cases.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: All attached blades are the same, so רבי contradicts himself.
steps.terutzMaskana: Attached-from-the-start is invalid. Detached-then-attached is valid בדיעבד.

steps.title: Where do we see this difference?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for a source showing that the law really does tell apart 'attached from the start' and 'detached then attached.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And from where do you say that there is a difference for us between something attached from the start and something detached and later attached?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for proof of the difference it just used. This sets up the ברייתא in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in step 21 depends on a difference that hasn't been proven yet. The גמרא wants a source showing that this difference really exists in the laws of שחיטה.

keyTerms.meaning: And from where do you say this? (a request for a source)
It makes a difference for us

phrases.english: And from where do you say
that there is a difference for us between something attached from the start
and something detached and in the end attached?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for a source for the difference used in step 21.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing the law treats attached-from-the-start differently from detached-then-attached.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows the difference
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that a knife stuck into a wall is valid, but a flint growing out of a wall or a reed growing by itself is invalid.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught in a ברייתא: One who slaughters with a wheel mechanism, his slaughter is valid. With something attached to the ground, his slaughter is valid. If he stuck a knife into a wall and slaughtered with it, his slaughter is valid. If a flint was sticking out of a wall, or a reed came up by itself, and he slaughtered with it, his slaughter is invalid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to prove that 'detached then attached' and 'attached from the start' are treated differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A knife stuck into a wall was loose first and then attached, and the ruling is valid. A flint that is naturally part of the wall, or a reed growing on its own, was attached from the start, and the ruling is invalid. This is exactly the difference step 21 used.

keyTerms.meaning: A mechanism, like a wheel with a knife fixed to it
He stuck it in / embedded it
A flint stone
A reed growing up on its own
His slaughter is invalid

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא proves the rule: knife stuck into a wall is valid (detached then attached); a flint or reed that grew there is invalid (attached from the start).
steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא is the source for the key difference that lets רבי's two rulings fit together.

phrases.english: As it was taught in a baraita: One who slaughters with a mechanism,
phrases.notes: Picture a turning wheel with a knife fixed onto it.

phrases.english: his slaughter is valid;
with something attached to the ground, his slaughter is valid;
phrases.notes: This can't mean something that grew there, because the end of the ברייתא rules that invalid. It means a loose blade later fixed to the ground.

phrases.english: if he stuck a knife into a wall and slaughtered with it,
his slaughter is valid;
phrases.notes: The knife was loose first and then fixed in place: detached then attached.

phrases.english: if there was a flint sticking out of the wall

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ קָנֶה עוֹלֶה מֵאֵלָיו וְשָׁחַט בּוֹ –
phrases.english: or a reed growing up on its own, and he slaughtered with it,
his slaughter is invalid.
phrases.notes: These were part of the wall or ground from the start, so they are invalid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 22 with a proof from a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: The difference between attached-from-the-start and detached-then-attached.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: a knife stuck into a wall is valid; a flint from a wall or a self-growing reed is invalid.
